title: The tunnelling current is exquisitely sensitive to the gap
caption: For φ = 4.5 eV, κ = √(2mφ)/ħ ≈ 10.9 nm⁻¹ and I ∝ e^(−2κd). Retracting the tip by only 0.1 nm multiplies the current by e^(−2.2) ≈ 0.11: about 9× smaller. That sensitivity is what lets an STM feel individual atoms.
alt: Relative tunnelling current against increase in gap from 0 to 0.3 nanometres: an exponential decay from 1 that has fallen to 0.11 at 0.1 nanometre and about 0.01 at 0.2.
description: Gap increase Δd = 0.1 nm: I/I₀ = e^(−2κΔd) = e^(−2.17) ≈ 0.11, about 9× smaller.
Δd = 0.2 nm: 0.013; each 0.1 nm costs about a factor of 9.
